start.text: A quay of pale dressed stone, and a sea wall running away from it both ways round the island, and on the wall, a hand apart, candles. Hundreds. Tallow stubs and fresh ones, burning in the still air, old wax run down the stone in long pale tongues.

Steps climb from the quay between more candles to a long hall of the same pale stone, every tall window lit. Above it, on the crown of the island, a squat beacon-tower, dark. And just past the candles, all the way round, the fog stands and does not come in, like a crowd at a door.
A young man in a short brown robe stands by the quay bell with its rope still in his hand and a lighting taper in the other, looking at your ember the way children look at the sea.
You're— that's— is that it? In your hand? Could I— no. No, I mustn't. The Provost said.
Brother Tobin Ashe. Porter. Welcome to Kindleby, Wakebearer. I'm to take you up. I mean, I'm to tell you she'll see you. I mean— the Provost's at the chapter-house. Up the steps.
Go on. I'll lie here. Mind they don't keep you.
